thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: RateLimiter: tenant=mosaic-health (VPC) — 429s spike detected in us-west-2 dedicated pool 'mosaic-dedicated-1'. 75% of requests returning 429 over last 5m. Paging on-call: @eli_sre.
eli_sre: taking. copying in ops. what's the visible customer impact?
karla-cs: Karla (CS) here — Mosaic reports users seeing failed payments and webhook retries, their frontend shows payment flow errors. Customer impact: checkout failures for ~20% of sessions. They escalated to their SRE and are on standby.
maya-g: adding logs from the ingress layer — see snippet: ```json
{"ts":"2026-03-15T14:02:16Z","tenant":"mosaic-health","status":429,"route":"/v1/generate","count":1280} 
{"ts":"2026-03-15T14:02:17Z","tenant":"mosaic-health","status":429,"error":"RateLimitExceeded"}```
samir-sre: looks like token bucket exhausted on the dedicated pool token ring. Metrics: burst window breached, queue length spiked to 18k. No obvious host OOM.
eli_sre: can we confirm whether this is noisy tenant or legitimate spike from Mosaic? If it's legitimate, they may need emergency uplift. If noisy, we isolate.
maya-g: traffic shows a sudden increase from a single IP block owned by mosaic's partner integration. It's logical traffic from them — not attacker. 95% of requests are valid.
keith-eng: quick options: 1) issue temporary rate override for tenant in control plane (1h), 2) divert their traffic to warm standby pool, 3) scale dedicated pool GPUs (slow, needs infra). Which path do we prefer?
eli_sre: prioritize fastest: temporary rate override while we shift some capacity. Maya — can you open warm pool routing for mosaic? ops-bot, any automation?
ops-bot: warm-pool-route: initiating allocation for 'mosaic-warm-1' (GPUs: 4xA10G) — expected ready in ~5m.
maya-g: routing rule prepared, need control-plane flag flip. Command: ```sh
redwood config route set --tenant mosaic-health --route pool=mosaic-warm-1 --drain 30s```
eli_sre: don't flip until we've granted short override, otherwise customers keep hitting 429 while warm pool spins. keith, can you draft override?
keith-eng: drafting override now. CLI: ```sh
redwood admin rate-override --tenant mosaic-health --limit 1500rps --window 60s --expires 2026-03-15T15:02:00Z --reason "Emergency uplift — customer-critical checkout failures"```
deploy-bot: rate-override request received. Requires billing sign-off for >1000rps sustained. Notifying @keith-eng, @finance.
keith-eng: pinging finance via ticket #FIN-1127 — request: emergency uplift for Mosaic for 1h while SRE migrates traffic.
karla-cs: I've told Mosaic we're working an emergency fix and requested patience. They asked for ETA ~10-15m.
samir-sre: while waiting, adding temporary policy to prefer cached responses and reduce model size for non-critical endpoints. Patch applied to canary.
eli_sre: approve rate override once finance responds. In parallel, I'll start traffic migration plan. Maya, prepare canary verification steps (latency, success rate).
maya-g: canary checks: 200 OKs for /v1/generate, token success >98%, tail latency <300ms for 90th pct. I'll post results.
keith-eng: finance approved emergency uplift under delegated authority (audit log created). Proceed with CLI.
keith-eng: running override now. ```sh
redwood admin rate-override --tenant mosaic-health --limit 1500rps --window 60s --duration 1h --reason "Emergency uplift" --operator keith-eng```
incident-bot: ACTION: rate-override applied for tenant=mosaic-health — limit 1500rps, expires in 1h. Audit ID: AR-20260315-0912.
maya-g: warm pool is reporting healthy and accepting traffic. Starting gradual 20% traffic shift.
eli_sre: verify logs.
maya-g: after 20% shift: 429 rate dropped from 75% -> 28%. After 60% shift: 429 rate at 4%. Canary metrics: success 98.6%, avg latency 220ms.
karla-cs: Mosaic product team confirms checkout errors much reduced, end-users reporting successful payments back online. They asked for postmortem and why this spike passed through.
samir-sre: root cause hypothesis: partner integration released a backfill job that caused sustained high RPS. Pool provisioning and token-bucket parameters didn't anticipate that pattern.
eli_sre: next steps: 1) keep override for 1h while keep warm pool routing in place, 2) follow-up runbook update to add auto-burst policy for enterprise VPCs with commerce SLAs, 3) CS to coordinate contract addendum for permanent higher burst or reserved capacity.
keith-eng: I created ticket ENG-9876 to add auto-burst config and a telem alert if tenant burst >50% of reserved for >3m.
karla-cs: I'll schedule the customer call in 1h to walk through mitigation and ask about capacity commitment.
maya-g: will capture detailed logs and attach to postmortem.
eli_sre: handing off long-tail monitoring to @samir-sre. If any regressions, page me.
samir-sre: taking second-shift monitoring. I'll keep eye on queue length, host load, and token refill rates.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation complete, customer impact significantly reduced. Monitoring window started.
eli_sre: closing the active paging handoff here. Thank you all. Quick retrospective later today — assign owners.
keith-eng: assigning follow-ups: ENG-9876 (auto-burst), FIN-1127 (billing addendum), CS-401 (customer call).
karla-cs: thanks team. Mosaic thanked us on the thread. :white_check_mark:
